records.issue_text: url and feed title/content interpolated unescaped into HTML strings in topic_embed.rb, allowing attribute breakout and markup injection via crafted feed entries
records.rationale: In `app/models/topic_embed.rb`, `TopicEmbed.import` appends `contents << "... #{url}"` with `url` interpolated directly into an HTML attribute and text without escaping. The only validation is `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which still allows quotes/markup (e.g. `http://x.com' onmouseover='...`). records.issue_text: No rescue around open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) in poll_feed.rb, so network errors kill the job with retry: false
records.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` has no error handling, so network/HTTP/open-uri exceptions will raise and cause the scheduled job run to fail. This is a concrete robustness/operational concern, and `sidekiq_options retry: false` means Sidekiq won’t auto-retry that failed execution.

records.issue_text: absolutize_urls drops the port for explicit default ports with non-matching scheme (http://host:443, https://host:80) and ignores protocol-relative and fragment/query-only relative URLs, leaving links broken
records.rationale: In TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls, the port is only appended when uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443, ignoring the scheme. This will incorrectly drop explicitly-specified non-default ports for the scheme (e.g., http://host:443 or https://host:80) because 443/80 are treated as always-default. records.issue_text: topic_embed_spec.rb asserts post.cooked.start_with?(...) which passes even if extra content is appended; no spec covers XSS in imported content or the raw_html default column value
records.rationale: The spec in `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb` uses `post.cooked.start_with?(...)`, which would still pass if the cooked HTML has unexpected/unsafe content appended, so it’s a concrete test weakness visible in the diff. Also, the diff introduces a new rendering bypass (`Post#cook` returns `raw` when `cook_method == :raw_html`) and a new DB default (`add_column :posts, :cook_method, ... default: 1`)

records.issue_text: content_sha1 is computed from pre-absolutize_urls content while the stored post contains absolutized content, causing sha mismatches and spurious revisions when URL scheme/port changes
records.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, `content_sha1` is computed from `contents` (after appending the “imported_from” footer) and stored on the `topic_embeds` row; on subsequent imports, the same computation is repeated and compared to `embed.content_sha1`. The stored post content is `absolutize_urls(url, contents)`, but the SHA is *consistently* based on the pre-absolutized `contents` on both create and update
